subject: Hosted→Dedicated sanity pulse & staged blackout plan

Cc: Darren Li <darren.li@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing validation and cutover sequencing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're narrowing in on committed capacity decisions and need a practical timeline for the hosted -> dedicated swap that includes: sizing validation (smoke/stress), a staging smoke window, and a small blackout/rollback plan. Can you share what Redwood typically runs for a deal our size (rough numbers for GPUs, expected peak rps, and KV cache sizing), and an example cutover cadence?

Attached is our traffic profile (v2) — it has the week/day/hour distribution and a couple of synthetic burst tests we ran. We also need an estimate for how long a warm-swap rehearsal and a production swap would take (including DNS and routing switch).

Goal: target a late-June go-live but willing to shift if the validation runway requires more time.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Data & ML, Aurelia Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing validation and cutover sequencing

Hi Sara — thanks for the profile, it was helpful. High level answers up front then the team will follow with specifics:

- Ballpark sizing for your traffic: 6-8x A100-40GB equivalent for baseline (steady state) with headroom for bursts via short-term burst slots; KV cache footprint estimated ~150GB (based on the average request context we saw in the CSV).
- Staging smoke: 2 phased smoke windows (internal rehearsal + customer-observed run) typically scheduled 7–10 days before production swap. Each smoke run ~2–4 hours.
- Production swap: we propose a 3-hour swap window with a 60-minute rollback hold; most customers complete routing cutover in ~20–40 minutes when pre-warmed and with prefix cache priming.

I'll ask SooJin to confirm kernel/quantization recommendations and Ben to propose the staging schedule and blackout/rollback details. If late-June is the goal, we should lock the rehearsal week by end of next week.

Jonas
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: SooJin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing validation and cutover sequencing

Thanks for the details, Jonas. I dug into the CSV and synthetic bursts — a few quick notes and requests before we lock sizing: 

1) Peak shape: the bursts are short (<90s) but up to 6x baseline RPS. That argues for a sustained baseline pool (6x A100-40GB) + 2x burst slots that can be temporarily provisioned during windows.
2) Sequence length & KV: median context length is 420 tokens; recommend KV cache ~150GB (as Jonas noted) but allocate 220GB in staging to validate eviction patterns.
3) Model choice / quantization: for your accuracy targets, prefer the LLM-XL-rlq quantized profile we tested — it reduces memory pressure by ~30% with minimal delta in quality for your prompts. I'll attach our mutual-action plan draft that includes quantization and eval milestones.

Requested items from Aurelia before we finalize staging numbers:
- Confirm a 48-hour window to run traffic mirroring into staging (we need real traffic for cache warm-up).
- Share any heavy multimodal payload days (if you have them) so we can spot-check throughput.

SooJin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood
--- Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v3.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing validation and cutover sequencing

Hi all — operational comments and a proposed schedule: 

Operational assumptions:
- Region: us-west-2 (matches Aurelia's primary region).
- Dedicated pool will be pre-provisioned and warmed for 48–72 hours before the customer-observed smoke.
- We'll enable prefix/KV cache seeding via traffic mirroring (SooJin's request).

Proposed timeline (delta vs. Jonas above):
- Week T-3: Provision dedicated fleet (6 baseline + 2 burst reserved) and run internal capacity soak.
- Week T-2: Run 48-hr traffic mirror into staging for cache priming and run synthetic long-run stress for 12 hours overnight.
- T-10 days: Internal rehearsal (dry run of cutover, not customer-observed). ~3 hours.
- T-7 days: Customer-observed staging smoke (two 2-hr windows spaced 24 hours apart).
- Production swap day: 03:00–06:00 UTC window (3 hours). 60-minute rollback hold.

Rollback plan (short):
- If latency or error rate exceeds threshold after prefix switch, rollback routing to hosted API and mark dedicated nodes for investigation. Full rollback should take <60 minutes.

Blackout considerations:
- We recommend a short customer-facing notice window (30 min) for any expected user-visible regression during the immediate cutover — most of the heavy backend work is invisible but DNS propagation for some integrations may take longer.

Attachments: I included an ICS for the proposed staging smoke windows (staging-smoke-window.ics). I'm flexible on exact times — flag any conflicts.

-Ben
Senior Infrastructure, Redwood
